messages:
maya: Quick handoff — I captured an nsys trace + torch.profiler snapshot for the r102 latency regression. s3: s3://redwood-profiling/1869999999/ (nsys.qdrep, torch_profiler.json, raw_logs.tar.gz). Looking for someone to sanity-check: 1) KV cache hit pattern, 2) big memcpy ops, 3) flamegraph anomalies. I ran on p4d-24 with batch_size=8. Details below.

aaron: Can you paste the exact reproduce command + git sha? Also, ps — did you include the sanitized inputs?

maya: git sha: b3a9f2d. Command I used: ```bash
./perf/run_benchmark.sh --model redwood-v1 --batch 8 --seq 1024 --profile nsys --out s3://redwood-profiling/1869999999/
```
Also ran the torch profiler with CPU+CUDA activities: `python -m torch.profiler --activities=CPU,CUDA --schedule=wait,warmup,active,repeat --output=torch_profiler.json`. Inputs are synthetic; customer ids scrubbed.

kai: I'll take a look. Quick note — torch.profiler's cuda_memory_snapshot can be noisy if memory pool is active. I'll convert the qdrep -> timeline and run our flamegraph pipeline. ETA ~45m :coffee:

perf-ci: Perf indicators: p95 latency +12% vs baseline. Artifacts: https://s3.redwood.com/1869999999/index.html (nsys.qdrep, timeline.sqlite, flame_1869999999.svg).

sasha: FYI make sure to scrub KV cache keys — they can leak hashed ids. Run `./scripts/scrub_trace.py --kv-only` before sharing externally. Also check that IPs are removed.

kai: Conversion steps I ran: ```bash
nsys export --input nsys.qdrep --output timeline.sqlite
python tools/nsys_to_flame.py timeline.sqlite > flame_1869999999.svg
```
Quick findings: large memcpy in `nvls` kernel ~120ms around step 23. Also a hot spot in `embedding_lookup` (CUDA) that lines up with KV evictions. Uploaded flame: https://perf.redwood.internal/flame/1869999999.svg :eyes:

maya: awesome, can you add a short note to PERF-874 and attach the flamegraph + raw traces? I'll create a follow-up canary if we decide on a mitigation. Thanks!

aaron: pinging @eng-oncall to confirm there were no infra hiccups during the capture window.

eng-oncall: No infra events detected between 2029-05-01T12:20Z and 2029-05-01T13:00Z. No node restarts or high host CPU flagged.

kai: small experiment: disabling cuDNN heuristics (CUDNN_USE_AUTOTUNE=0) on a quick local run reduced the memcpy spike by ~80%. Suggest running a dedicated canary with that env var toggled on the dedicated fleet.

maya: I'll schedule the canary tomorrow morning on the dedicated pool and post results here. Closing the handoff for now — thanks everyone :thumbsup:
